deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to Gauss's induction experiments with Weber's magnetometer (c. 1834–35). For each of three series it lists 12 scale readings a_0..a_11 taken at equal intervals. The labels are '1. P.O.', '2. P.U.' and '3. Ohne M.'. My guess is that P.O./P.U. mean 'Pol oben/unten' (pole up/down) and 'Ohne M.' means without the multiplier or magnet. That reading is not certain.

Pattern in the data: the even readings drift upward by about 130 per step and the odd readings drift downward by about 130. As a result, consecutive sums alternate between two near-constant levels (about 1885 and about 2015). The gap between the two levels is the quantity of interest, a_{2k+2}-a_{2k}, which is essentially the deflection shift per step.

The same procedure is applied to each series.

(1) Pair sums and differences.
- Column I, pairs (2k,2k+1): s_k = a_{2k}+a_{2k+1} and d_k = a_{2k+1}-a_{2k}, for k=0..5.
- Column II, pairs (2k+1,2k+2): s'_k = a_{2k+1}+a_{2k+2} and d'_k = a_{2k+2}-a_{2k+1}, for k=0..4.
- Example (P.O.): 612.3+1271.8=1884.1, difference 659.5; 1271.8+749.1=2020.9, difference -522.7; and so on.

(2) Means.
- P.O.: mean s = 11313.9/6 = 1885.650; mean d = 16.1/6 ≈ 2.7 (using Gauss's -624.0). Mean s' = 10080.9/5 = 2016.180; mean d' = 12.3/5 ≈ 2.45.
- P.U.: mean s = 1885.133, mean d written as -67.4; mean s' = 2011.060, mean d' = 69.3.
- Ohne M.: mean s = 1874.70, mean d = -72.7; mean s' = 2002.60, mean d' = 74.9.

(3) Empirical drift coefficient x.
- The sums drift linearly against the differences. Gauss models this as s = S - x·d. This is the 'x' on the page, and the sign follows from the data (my reconstruction).
- He estimates x from the end values: x = (|s_end - s_0| + |s'_end - s'_0|) / (|d_0| + |d_end| + |d'_0| + |d'_end|).
- P.O.: 1.3 = 1885.4-1884.1 and 9.4 = 2020.9-2011.5. Also 1283.5 = 659.5+624.0 and 1040.6 = 522.7+517.9. So 10.7/2324.1 = 1/217.2.
- P.U.: 0.8 and 8.8 against 1257.8 and 1004.0, giving 9.6/2261.8 = 1/235.6.
- Ohne M.: 3.9 and 6.8 against 1278.3 and 1020.8, giving 10.7/2299.1 = 1/214.9.

(4) Reduced levels and their gap.
- The reduced levels are S = mean s + x·mean d and S' = mean s' + x·mean d'.
- The gap is S'-S = (mean s' - mean s) + (mean d' - mean d)·x.
- P.U.: 125.867 + 136.7x, with 136.7/235.6 = 0.580, giving 126.447.
- Ohne M.: 127.90 + 147.6x, with 147.6/214.9 = 0.687, giving 128.587.
- P.O.: 130.530 + 5.2x, with 5.2/217.2 = 0.024, giving 130.554.

The previous and next pages apply the identical scheme to other series (e.g. 128.585, 93.104, 128.992, 128.796). The procedure is a routine reduction of oscillation readings: alternating rest positions corrected for a linear amplitude-dependent drift.
errors: P.O., row 5: 620.7-1264.7 = -644.0, but Gauss wrote -624.0 (the sum 1885.4 is correct). This propagates into mean d (should be -3.9/6 = -0.65, not +2.7) and into x (should be 10.7/2344.1 = 1/219.1).

P.O., combination step: with his own values, S'-S should be 130.530 + (2.45-2.7)x = 130.530 - 0.25x. He wrote +5.2x, adding the coefficients instead of subtracting, which is inconsistent with his treatment of P.U. and Ohne M. With the corrected -644.0 the coefficient becomes 2.46+0.65 = 3.11, giving 130.530+0.014 = 130.544. His 130.554 is off by only 0.01.
P.U.: 2011.060 - 1885.133 = 125.927, not 125.867 as written. The final value should therefore be about 126.507 rather than 126.447.
P.U.: the mean of the column-I differences is -406.4/6 = -67.73, not -67.4. This has negligible effect: the coefficient becomes 137.0 and the correction 0.581.
Ohne M. section: all arithmetic checks.

results.what: Reduction of equally spaced magnetometer readings to two alternating rest positions. Pair sums and differences are formed, and a linear correction of the sums proportional to the pair difference (coefficient estimated from end values) is applied before taking the gap.
results.modern_name: Ad hoc linear drift/amplitude correction of oscillation turning-point data (cf. Gauss–Weber magnetometer reduction, multiplication/recoil methods)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber, magnetometer methods of the 1830s

deep.surprise_reason: Routine numerical reduction of laboratory readings in Gauss's well-documented induction experiments. It is interesting only for its bookkeeping and two small arithmetic slips.

checkable.asserts: with Gauss's -624.0 the mean difference is about 2.68 (2.7x)

transcription_corrections: P.O. col I: '1885.650 + 2.7x' has an overwritten sign; '245x' means 2.45x.
P.O. row 5 col I: the manuscript shows -624.0 with an overwritten digit; the correct difference is -644.0.
P.O. right block: the 1/x values are written beneath as '217,2'; '24' means 0.024.
P.U. row 1 col II: the difference is likely -180.3 rather than -180.0 (1096.8+916.5=2013.3 and 916.5-1096.8=-180.3).
Ohne M.: '687' means 0.687; '128,587' means 128.587; '214.9' is the value of 1/x.
